newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wrightson sees savings through restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Wrightson sees savings through restructuring.

text.p: Wrightson Ltd chief executive Greg Kay said on Thursday the company's restructuring programme, dubbed "Project Transformation", was making good progress and the company was well on the way towards achieving annualised savings of NZ$8-9 million.

Kay told shareholders at the company's annual meeting: "In June this year, we announced that we would be reducing staff by 18 percent over a 12 to 18 month period, centralising our administration or 'back office' processes, streamlining our asset base by exiting from surplus properties and unloading underperforming or non-core businesses."
"Allied with this, we are introducing a range of new technological solutions designed to make the company more efficient and easier to do business with."
Kay said to cover the costs of these changes, the company had made a one-off restructuring provision of NZ$17.5 million at the end of the financial year under review.
"I can report that we are making good progress in implementing these changes and are well on the way toward achieving annualised savings of NZ$8-9 million."

Kay said that as a consequence of increasing the size of its grain and seed business through the acquisition of Hodder and Tolley Ltd, the company had now achieved a strong market position and was well placed to grow in New Zealand and overseas.
